clue.text: US tourist area’s carbon copy hoax

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to ape is to copy or mimic
cod is British slang for a hoax or sham

explanation.surface: A rumour that some American holiday spot is just a fake copy of somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has' or 'is' joining definition to wordplay. Cod as an adjective or noun means a fake or a hoax in British usage, as in 'cod science'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Cod is a peninsula in Massachusetts famous as a summer holiday destination for Americans.

clue.text: Agents interrupted by rogue, noisy male?

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing breaking into its middle, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, whose staff are agents
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue

explanation.surface: Spies whose operation is broken up by a loud-mouthed scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisy male' sounds like a description of the rogue, but it is the definition; the question mark flags that it is a description by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Only male cicadas produce the loud buzzing song for which the insects are known, so a noisy male is one.

clue.text: Specialist Guardian/Telegraph leader writer

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: a pro, or professional, is a specialist
this puzzle runs in the Guardian, so the paper speaking of itself says 'us'
first letter of Telegraph

explanation.surface: A columnist who writes the editorials for two rival British newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'leader writer' as an editorial writer; in fact 'leader' takes only the first letter of Telegraph and 'writer' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was a French novelist, author of In Search of Lost Time, so he is a famous writer.

clue.text: Junk and smack following fish south

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this piece is placed behind the others

blocks.note: the cod is a common food fish
S is the compass abbreviation for south
a wallop is a heavy blow, a smack

explanation.surface: A sailing junk and a fishing smack heading south after a shoal.
explanation.walkthrough: Junk and smack both look like boats (a smack is a fishing vessel), but one is the definition and the other a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for nonsense, and junk can mean worthless rubbish or nonsense talk.

clue.text: Explosive red gas without a residue

indicators.note: to be without something is to lack it, so a letter is taken out
an explosion blows things apart, so the letters scatter and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word gas with its A removed
the letter taken out of gas

explanation.surface: A red gas that blows up without leaving any trace behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive red gas' looks like a chemistry description; 'Explosive' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment or leftover remains at the bottom of a container, i.e. a residue.

clue.text: Fun right to the end, like a god

indicators.note: sending something to the end removes it from its place and puts it last

blocks.note: mirth is fun; its R is lifted out of the middle
R is the abbreviation for right; it is put back at the end
as means like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: Having a great time right through to the finish, as carefree as a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: MIRTH has its R moved to the back to give MITHR, then AS is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Mithras was a deity worshipped in a mystery cult popular among Roman soldiers.

clue.text: Microwave part (foreign – not German)

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters come out in an alien order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A component of a microwave oven, labelled as imported but not made in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads like a note on the part's origin; in fact 'foreign' rearranges the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetron is the vacuum tube that generates the microwaves inside a microwave oven.

clue.text: Purloined jumper and tracksuit top came to be settled

indicators.note: the top of a word written down is its opening letter

blocks.note: to purloin is to steal, i.e. took
a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper
first letter of tracksuit

explanation.surface: Someone stole a sweater and a tracksuit top, then decided to stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is British for a sweater, which suits the tracksuit picture, but here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: To take root is to become established in a place, as a plant does, so the idiom means came to be settled.

clue.text: Check on stock

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
stock in the sense of lineage or breed is a strain

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's reminder to look over the inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check on stock' reads as a stocktaking instruction; check is the verb to hold back, and stock is ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, the same as to restrain it.

clue.text: Like Pagliacci touching female star on date

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so this piece comes after

blocks.note: touching in the sense of moving or poignant, i.e. sad
F is the abbreviation for female
an ace is a star performer
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: An opera fan finding Pagliacci moving, with its leading lady on opening night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' reads as a link meaning 'concerning'; it is the adjective for something moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagliacci is Leoncavallo's opera about clowns; its hero Canio is the classic weeping clown, with a mournful painted expression.

clue.text: Could rocks darken?

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so the letters are jolted into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether stones are capable of turning a darker colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like the noun, stones; it is the verb, shakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloud something is to make it dim or gloomy, as when clouds cover the sun, so it means darken.

clue.text: Object about obscene gesture – finally arrested

indicators.note: what comes finally is at the end, so the closing letter is taken
about means around, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: an end is an aim or object, as in 'to that end'
gross means coarse or obscene
last letter of gesture

explanation.surface: A complaint about a rude hand sign that finally led to someone's arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscene gesture' reads as one thing, but 'obscene' and 'gesture' feed separate pieces; arrested means held, as attention is.
explanation.definitionFit: An arresting sight holds attention; to be arrested in that sense is to be absorbed or gripped, i.e. engrossed.

clue.text: Fit type used to be female’s kitchen aid

blocks.note: a dish is an attractive person, and fit is British slang for attractive
was is the past tense of be
her is the female possessive

explanation.surface: A woman's mixer or blender that used to be a sturdy model.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a fit person is a good-looking one, also called a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishwasher is a domestic appliance that cleans plates and pans, a helpful kitchen machine.

clue.text: A killer in the main section of motorcade

indicators.note: a section is a part cut out of a whole, so the letters lie within the next word

blocks.note: the letters run inside this word

explanation.surface: An assassin lurking in the central part of a presidential convoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is a poetic word for the sea, so the killer is at sea, not in the car procession.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is the killer whale, a predator found in oceans, i.e. a killer living in the sea.

clue.text: On the radio, one croons ‘Darling’ which might be piped

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than read, so the words count by their sound

blocks.note: one is I, croons is sing, and Darling is the endearment sugar

explanation.surface: A crooner on the wireless performs a love song that might be played through speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piped' suggests piped music, but it is the baker's piping bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing sugar is fine powdered sugar mixed into icing that bakers squeeze through a nozzle to decorate cakes.

clue.text: Vital sack for heater

blocks.note: vital in the sense of lively and thrilling, i.e. electric
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: An essential bag to carry a stove in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like a bag; it is the verb to dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric fire is a British name for an electric room heater with glowing bars.

clue.text: Resort area lawyer’s overwhelmed by ‘pathetic zero cut’

indicators.note: something pathetic is in a sorry, broken state, so the letters are muddled
to be overwhelmed is to be swamped and surrounded, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer at a resort swamped by complaints about a miserable pay cut to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is': the lawyer is overwhelmed, i.e. sits inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Côte d'Azur is the French Riviera, a Mediterranean coastline lined with holiday towns such as Nice and Cannes.

clue.text: Gave credit to a dead writer taking centre place

indicators.note: whatever takes the centre place sits in the middle, inside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
a scribe is a writer
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Honouring a late author by putting them centre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead writer' reads as one figure; the two words feed separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe something to someone is to attribute it, so ascribed means credited with or gave credit to.

clue.text: Wayward sailor working up marines a lot at first

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
what comes at first is the opening, so only the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
on means working, as a machine is on
RM stands for the Royal Marines
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An unruly seaman winding up the marines a great deal from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working up' looks like the phrasal verb to provoke; 'up' simply reverses the word for working.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayward means unpredictable or departing from the usual course, so it is near in sense to abnormal or deviant.

clue.text: Bent on cuts in organisation, India?

indicators.note: organising means arranging, so the letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is India determined to make spending cuts within some organisation?
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the letters to rearrange; the question mark signals that India is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian subcontinent is a large landmass of South Asia, often simply called the subcontinent, with India its chief country.

clue.text: Bond in southern state – he scored!

indicators.note: to be in something is to be held within it

blocks.note: GA is the abbreviation for Georgia, a southern US state
a link is a bond or connection

explanation.surface: James Bond in a Deep South state, celebrating after a goal or a conquest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' sounds like sport or romance, but it means wrote a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka was a Russian composer, so he is someone who wrote music, i.e. scored.

clue.text: Like breaking outside power with English spirit

indicators.note: breaking smashes something apart, so the letters are reassembled differently
to be outside something is to surround it

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the symbol for power in physics
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Something like an English spirit breaking free of its constraints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' adds the final letter after the container is built.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish folklore a kelpie is a water spirit that takes the form of a horse, so a supernatural being.

clue.text: See 6 Down
American academic feels sad for flighty thing

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
someone who feels sad is blue

explanation.surface: A US professor who feels down about a frivolous, flighty person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty thing' reads as a fickle person; it is literally something that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adonis blue is a vivid blue European butterfly, and a butterfly is a creature of flight.

clue.text: Poor Miss ‘Y’

blocks.note: to miss something is to need or lack it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pity the unfortunate young woman known only as Miss Y.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a title for a woman; it is the verb meaning to lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy people lack money and necessities, so the adjective means poor or impoverished.

clue.text: Wally gets told off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A silly person receives a scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads as one phrase meaning scolded; 'off' is the signal to rearrange. A wally is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A wally is a foolish, inept person, and a dolt is a stupid person, so both are synonyms for idiot.

clue.text: Gull menagerie’s back in British promenade

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters run in reverse
to be in something is to be held inside it

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
to promenade is to stroll, to amble
a menagerie is a collection of animals, a zoo

explanation.surface: A seagull from the zoo is back on a seaside promenade in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gull' looks like the seabird, fitting a promenade; it is the verb to dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to trick or deceive them, and to bamboozle is likewise to fool or hoodwink.

clue.text: Brief from short officer on horseback

indicators.note: something short has been cut down, so the word loses its tail

blocks.note: a general is an officer, shortened to its first three letters
a jockey who is up is riding a horse

explanation.surface: Instructions from a small cavalry officer riding into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like the noun, a set of instructions; it is the verb, to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: To gen up is British informal for to inform or get informed, so it means to brief someone.

clue.text: It expands crude oil trade endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
something crude is rough and unrefined, so the letters are not yet in proper order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A business that grows the trade in unrefined petroleum forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude oil' reads as one thing, petroleum; 'crude' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilator is a muscle or instrument that widens an opening, so it is something that expands.

clue.text: Police force decline to give area in imperial terms

blocks.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: A police force refusing to measure its territory in old units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refuse; it is the verb to deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a measurement in yards, a unit of the old British system, so it expresses size in non-metric units.
